sites.operation: STG.E [R18.64], R13 (st.global.f32, SASS 0x2000; executed by every thread with foundKValue)
STG.E.64 [R16.64], R24 (st.global.s64, SASS 0x2010; executed by every thread with foundKValue)

thread_pair_example: driver input: one slice of 4096 equal elements (0.0f), k = 5, launch <<<1, 1024>>>: every thread's first element (i = threadIdx.x) equals kValue, so all 1024 threads execute L85 and L86 on the same two global words (kthValue[0], indices[0]). E.g. block 0: thread 0 (warp 0) and thread 32 (warp 1) both store indices[0] at L86 (values 0 vs 32) and kthValue[0] at L85 (equal values). Each store site races with ITSELF as executed by another thread (WAW, the two sites are the two words of the same finding: L86 carries the observable nondeterminism, L85 stores identical values), also between lanes of one warp.
class_reason: Plain (non-atomic, non-volatile) global stores to one word from many threads of different warps (and lanes) with no barrier or other ordering between them; there is no strong/atomic access involved, so DR (not SC) under D20. The values written to kthValue[0] are identical but the indices written to indices[0] differ per thread, so the surviving index is arbitrary (smoke run on sm_75: index=208 instead of 0).
buggy_expected: WAW on the global words kthValue[slice] (L85) and indices[slice] (L86), reported as DR between different threads of block 0, cross-warp (and intra-warp pairs as well)

residual_sites.operation: LDS R5, [0x80] (ld.shared.s32 of the __shared__ int32_t minIndexFound; SASS 0x1ea0 in the fixed driver)
REDUX.MIN.S32 UR5,R24 / VOTEU.ANY / @P0 ATOMS.MIN.S32 RZ,[0x80],R0 (warp-aggregated shared atomicMin; SASS 0x2070-0x20c0 in the fixed driver)

fixed.reason: the fix removes the global WAW: each thread now atomicMin's its first match into the __shared__ minIndexFound (fixed L86), __syncthreads (fixed L91), and only thread 0 writes indices[0] and kthValue[0] (fixed L94-95). verify.expected_report_fixed: the WAW pair is gone; BUT the early-exit read `if (i >= minIndexFound)` (fixed L77, plain LDS) runs concurrently with other threads' atomicMin on the same shared word with no barrier in between: a plain-read vs atomic-RMW conflict, benign by design (the read only prunes the search; any stale value still yields the correct minimum), that a detector may report on the fixed commit (class DR by D20: one side is a plain access). The initialising store L71 (thread 0) is ordered before the loop by the barrier at L73, and the final read L94 follows the barrier at L91.
